reason: The hypothesis relies on Cr-rich precipitates improving ductility and irradiation tolerance, but the cited evidence (E3, E1) shows Cr-rich precipitates are associated with embrittlement and irradiation-enhanced precipitation, directly contradicting the proposed mechanism. The ductility improvement from fine phases is supported only by a non-refractory HEA (E4), not by refractory systems. The irradiation mechanism (E2) is from a different alloy system and does not involve Cr-induced precipitates as beneficial sinks.
premises: Cr addition to refractory HEAs can form Cr-rich precipitates
Cr-rich precipitates can be detrimental to mechanical properties (embrittlement)
Fine secondary phases can improve ductility and irradiation tolerance
He migration energy is higher in W-Ta-Cr-V than in pure W, leading to smaller, more uniform bubbles
Grain boundaries can act as defect sinks, improving irradiation resistance
